lessonPuzzle.backgroundText: Refrigerators slow down bacteria by keeping food at a lower temperature. That’s why leftovers last longer when they’re stored cold instead of sitting out.
lessonPuzzle.question: Why does food usually last longer in the refrigerator?
lessonPuzzle.successResponse: Correct. Clean answer. ✅ Next clue unlocked.

UIInfo.title: Temperature and Time
UIInfo.subtitle: Cold doesn’t stop biology—it slows it down.

lessonPuzzle.backgroundText: Microorganisms that spoil food multiply more slowly at low temperatures. Refrigeration reduces their reproduction rate, which is why perishable food lasts longer when kept cold.
lessonPuzzle.question: What’s the best explanation for why refrigeration helps preserve food?

answers.text: It slows microbial reproduction and spoilage
It removes all oxygen from the food
It increases chemical reactions in the food

lessonPuzzle.successResponse: Nice. That’s the science. 🔬 Next clue is live.
lessonPuzzle.failureResponse: Nope—close, but not it. Think: microbes + temperature + growth rate.

clueToNextTag.text: Next location is upstairs: the common bathroom. Zero mystery on the room, minor mystery on the placement. Look near the toilet—somewhere 'reachable' but not screaming for attention.
clueToNextTag.hint2: If you can hear a fan switch, you’re in the right neighborhood.
clueToNextTag.hint3: Near the toilet in the upstairs common bathroom.

lessonPuzzle.backgroundText: Refrigeration is risk control: it reduces the rate of microbial growth and slows enzymatic activity. In practical terms, cold storage extends safe usability and reduces spoilage.
lessonPuzzle.question: Which statement best captures why refrigeration preserves food?

answers.text: It slows microbial growth and enzymatic processes
It sterilizes food by killing all bacteria instantly
It makes food airtight by changing its chemistry
It increases fermentation to improve shelf life

lessonPuzzle.failureResponse: Incorrect. Reassess the mechanism: slowdown, not elimination. Try again.
